🚨 **BLOCKING: CI red on this commit — `agent_loop.dart` is now 2801 lines, over the 2800-line god-file ceiling**

The guards leg fails (`ci_failures.md` → "CRAP + duplication", job 140774142886):

```
[FAIL] loc: 1/732 files over their limit
  lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart: 2801 lines > max 2800
```

and the aggregate "Quality gate" fails in cascade (`Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (guards)`); "Binaries smoke gate", "JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" and the second "Quality gate" are red on the same commit with logs unavailable (404). Verified locally on head `2af9c58ad0`: `wc -l lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` → 2801.

The round-2 hunks (this `_findTool` fallback block + the transformContext comment) added ~19 lines to a file that was already at the ceiling — the added lines above are the direct cause. `AGENTS.md` fixes the ceiling at ≤ 2800 lines per `.dart` file (crap4dart `loc` gate), so CI stays red until the file is split.

Fix per `AGENTS.md` ("split by concern into `part` files — never by extracting public API"): move a self-contained section into a `part`/`part of` pair — the natural seams are the request-payload builders (`_buildRequestContext` and its rewrite helpers, ~200 lines) or the tool-call execution section (`_executeToolCalls`/`_prepareToolCall`/`_executePreparedToolCall`, all private). A ~20-line trim alone would also clear the gate but re-erodes on the next change; the split is the durable fix. (Minor, same fix: the new live-list search loop in `_findTool` duplicates the snapshot loop — fold it into a small `_nameIn(List<Tool>, String)` helper while restructuring.)

comments.author: ai-teammate
ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: executor routing still reads the run-start snapshot — schema and routing agree only through the CLI's `missingToolResolver`**

This field fixes the *payload* half of gh-2458 (the outbound `Context.tools`), but the loop's own routing half is unchanged and still bound to the run-start snapshot:

- `_prepareToolCall` (`agent_loop.dart:2341`) resolves an incoming `tool_use` via `_findTool(context, name)` → `context.tools`, where `context` is the run-start transcript snapshot (`Agent._createContextSnapshot`, `agent.dart:858-864`); the gate's `apply()` re-syncs `agent.state.tools`, a different object, so the mounted tool is never found there.
- On a miss the only fallback is `config.missingToolResolver` (`agent_loop.dart:2345-2349`) → error result `Tool X not found` at `:2350`. The sequential-mode probe has the same snapshot lookup (`:2156`).
- The executor is never reached for a snapshot-missing name — wrapping via `wrapExecutor` cannot route it, because the existence check gates execution first.

Only `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:1087` installs a resolver. `ToolAvailabilityGate` and `othersTool` are public barrel exports (`lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart:329-330`), so an SDK host wiring discovery per the gate's own docs — gate + `othersTool` + `wrapExecutor`, no resolver — now gets the mounted tool *advertised* in the schema and then a hard `Tool agent_message not found` when the model calls it. That is worse than pre-PR (before, the tool was never advertised so the model never called it): the schema half and the routing half disagree, exactly what the ticket acceptance forbids ("root cause fixed at the mechanism level — schema visibility AND executor routing AND `_mounted` bookkeeping agree after a mid-loop mount"). The new tests pass only because every routing case (`_runMountThenCall`, the Agent-wiring test) installs a resolver, which masks the gap.

Fix suggestion: when the snapshot lookup misses and `config.toolsProvider` is installed, let `_findTool` fall back to the live list (`config.toolsProvider?.call()`), and add one test that mounts mid-loop *without* a resolver and asserts the call routes to the executor. This keeps the honest no-resolver contract for genuinely un-mounted tools (the #680 tombstone) while making the mounted case agree at the loop layer for all hosts, not just the CLI.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT — fixed**

The `transformContext` rebuild in `_buildRequestContext` now threads `tools: requestContext.tools` instead of the run-start `context.tools` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart:1737`). The `liveTools` rewrite runs first, so when `toolsProvider` returned a list the rebuild now carries that live list forward; with no provider installed it falls back to the snapshot, unchanged.

- **Test**: `test/agent/gh2458_midloop_mount_test.dart` — new case *"(b2) REVIEW: a transformContext hook must not clobber the live-tools rewrite"*: `_runMountThenCall` now accepts a `transformContext` hook; the rig mounts `agent_message` mid-loop with the hook installed alongside `toolsProvider` and asserts request 2's tools array contains the mounted tool. Red first (request 2 showed only `read`/`others`), green after the one-line fix.
- All 7 tests in the suite pass; `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` and `dart analyze` clean.

comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT — fixed**

Routing now agrees with the schema at the loop layer, not only through the CLI's `missingToolResolver`:

- `agent_loop.dart` `_findTool(context, name)` gained an optional `AgentLoopConfig? config` parameter: after the run-start snapshot misses, it falls back to `config.toolsProvider?.call()` — the same per-request live list the schema half already consults (`agent.state.tools`, re-synced by `ToolAvailabilityGate.apply`/`mount`). `_prepareToolCall` (:2345), the sequential-mode probe (:2160), and the misuse-breaker `toolDescription` lookup all pass the config.
- The honest no-resolver contract is preserved: an *un-mounted* discoverable is in neither the snapshot nor the live list, so `_findTool` still misses → `missingToolResolver` (when installed) remains the last resort with its mount side effect → otherwise the plain `Tool X not found` / #680 tombstone path is untouched. The existing no-toolsProvider honesty case in this suite pins exactly that.
- **Test**: `test/agent/gh2458_midloop_mount_test.dart` — new case *"(b3) REVIEW: mounts mid-loop with NO resolver — the call routes to the executor, not the snapshot not-found"*: `_runMountThenCall(useResolver: false)` mounts `agent_message` mid-loop via `others` and asserts the `tool_use` reaches the executor (`agent_message executed`, no error). Red first ("Tool agent_message not found"), green after the fallback.

All 7 tests in the suite pass; `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` and `dart analyze` clean.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The gh-2458 root cause (run-start tool snapshot) is correctly fixed for the shipped CLI path and is well tested (5 new tests, all green), but two ⚠️ issues keep the mechanism incomplete: the new live-tools rewrite is silently clobbered when a host installs `transformContext`, and executor routing still resolves names against the run-start snapshot, so schema and routing agree only through the CLI's `missingToolResolver`.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ `agent_loop.dart:1730-1735` — the `transformContext` rebuild reads `tools: context.tools` (run-start snapshot), discarding the `liveTools` rewrite; any host with the public `Agent.transformContext` hook set reproduces gh-2458 verbatim.
- ⚠️ `agent_loop.dart:668` — `_prepareToolCall`/`_executeToolCalls` still route via `_findTool(currentContext)` on the snapshot; without the CLI-only resolver, a public-API gate host gets the tool advertised but "Tool X not found" on call.

**Next Steps**:
1. Thread `requestContext.tools` through the `transformContext` rebuild + add a test with a `transformContext` hook installed.
2. Add the live-list fallback to `_findTool` (or equivalent) + a no-resolver mount-then-call test.
3. Optional hardening: one REG pass mounting every demoted family through the real `Agent` wiring without a scripted resolver.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: Both round-1 ⚠️ findings are verifiably fixed in head `2af9c58ad0` (transformContext rebuild now threads `requestContext.tools`; `_findTool` falls back to the live `toolsProvider` list with the no-resolver honesty contract intact — 7/7 tests green, `dart analyze` clean), but CI is red on this commit: the rework hunks pushed `agent_loop.dart` to 2801 lines, one over the 2800-line `loc` gate ceiling, redding the guards leg and the "Quality gate" aggregate.

**Key Issues** (5 failed checks on commit `2af9c58a` — `ci_failures.md`):
- 🚨 **CRAP + duplication** — root cause: `loc` gate `[FAIL] lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart: 2801 lines > max 2800` (posted as inline thread; split by concern into `part` files per AGENTS.md).
- 🚨 **Quality gate** — cascade: `Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (guards)` (the loc failure above).
- 🚨 **Quality gate** (2nd check) — failed; job log unavailable (GitHub 404).
- 🚨 **Binaries smoke gate** — failed; job log unavailable (GitHub 404).
- 🚨 **JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)** — failed; job log unavailable (GitHub 404).

**Next Steps**:
1. Split `agent_loop.dart` under the ceiling (part-file split by concern — request-payload builders or tool-call execution are the natural seams); CI re-runs automatically.
2. Re-check the three log-unavailable failures after CI re-runs — if any stay red with logs, they are owned failures to fix in the next lap.
3. Digest (no thread, no ceiling impact once the split lands): `agent_loop.dart:2440-2445` — the `_findTool` live-list loop duplicates the snapshot search loop; fold into a tiny name-search helper while restructuring.
